verdict.rationale: Viam documents public APIs that are meant to be driven programmatically. The fleet management API manages machines "with code the same way you can do in the web UI," the machine API sends commands remotely through SDKs, and the CLI "can call any API method a machine serves, with JSON in and JSON out." An explicit guide covers using Viam from an AI agent. The OpenAPI probe returned 404 at every candidate path, but the APIs are documented through SDKs and the CLI rather than a REST spec, so this does not contradict the claim. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of API use, a machine-readable API spec (e.g. OpenAPI)

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The fleet management API allows you to manage your machine fleet with code the same way you can do in the web UI.
The machine API allows you to connect to your machine from within a supported Viam SDK, retrieve status information, and send commands remotely.
The CLI can call any API method a machine serves, with JSON in and JSON out; no code to write.
An AI agent with a shell or an SDK can operate a Viam machine the same way a person or a program can.
